tldr: On the maintained marginal, administratively complete Sobolev sensitivity class, an observable nonlinear temporal-borrowing estimator attains the exact all-procedure local minimax squared-error value \(R_G(P,B)\), uniformly on the declared compact positive \(C^1\) baseline domains and each bounded smooth nuisance set. The explicit Neumann estimator separately attains the optimal-linear value \(R_{\mathrm{lin}}(P,B)\). The clipping calculation is part of \texttt{thm:linear-frontier}: it proves \(R_G(P,B)\le R_{\mathrm{lin}}(P,B)-\epsilon_0(P,B)<R_{\mathrm{lin}}(P,B)\) for every \(0<B<\infty\), with a positive compact-domain certificate. The two observable risk limits in \texttt{thm:feasible-linear-risk} and \texttt{thm:feasible-gaussian-minimax} give the corresponding strict asymptotic worst-case scaled-MSE improvement. By \texttt{thm:boundary-regimes}, both curves equal \(V_0\) at exact transport and tend to \(V_T\) at the trial-only limit. Full temporal discrepancy also improves strictly on the specified Gaussian trial-contrast/unweighted-discrepancy restriction at the legal unequal-competing-hazard witness for a certified range including \(B=0.1\). The exact original-data terminal-summary comparison remains the unresolved \texttt{oeq:raw-compression}. At zero radius the model is a strict marginal smooth subclass of Su et al.; positive drift leaves exact transport. A covariate-adjusted right-censored clinical reanalysis requires a separate extension.
